163	#### A. Identity, layer and reads
164	
165	**HS-1. The HUD draws; it decides nothing.** *Rule.* The HUD is a `PRESENTATION` subscriber of the kernel's subscriber classes. It owns no block, hook, command, mutator, reading key, RNG stream or `INPUT_SURFACE`, and "the HUD's prompts do not [issue commands]". It writes only `CanvasItem`, `Material` and audio-request properties, never a block, command, camera or viewport property. Every *when* — a rung and its hold, `prompt_state`, `length_class`, the tick schedule, the lie stage, the save-failure count, alarm eligibility — is cited from its owner and never derived by the HUD. *Why.* The scope guard: the HUD is the scene-tree side of the kernel's rule that simulation systems stay scene-tree free. *Edge notes.* If a needed *when* has no owner (the ship-alarm source; the warmth band edges had no owner until SE-29 published them), the HUD raises an ASK (Open Questions) and draws nothing in the interim; it never invents the rule.
166	
167	**HS-2. Layer 2, in the root viewport.** *Rule.* The HUD is a `CanvasLayer` (layer 2, group `hud`) in the **root viewport**, never inside the 640 x 360 world `SubViewport`. It receives no world light, glow, ambient, occlusion, Filter pass, camera shake or jolt, by construction (a different viewport). The HUD scale `H` is an integer in `{H_default .. 2 * H_default}` (and, at MVP, in the `offered(P_w, P_h)` subset of it, D.8) with `H_default = max(k_auto, 3)` (`HUD_MIN_SCALE` 3; the Pipeline's PR-12 form: `k_auto` is the picture's automatic world scale, not the live zoom step `k`), independent of the world scale `k` and of the zoom ladder (`k` in `[1, k_auto + 2]`); *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* a zoom step or an `H` change alters no simulation value. No HUD code reads `k` or assumes `H == k`: its only scale inputs are `H` and the picture rect. *Why.* P1: the frame is an anchor. The Pipeline's two-integer-scales-in-one-window wiring (the Steam Deck: world 2x, HUD 3x) is an MVP requirement whose wiring is NOT SOURCEABLE until the Pipeline's spike step 11. *Edge notes.* A `Control` found under the world `SubViewport` fails the scene-tree lint (Pipeline lint (b)); in a release build it would receive world light and the Filter, so this is a build gate, not a runtime check.
168	
169	**HS-3. Frame register versus reading register.** *Rule.* Screen space has two registers. The **frame register** — plates, bezels, chamfers, rivets, keycaps, labels, the prompt plate, the bar, the rail glyphs and counts, the failed-write notice, the first-frame line, the focus bracket — is fed nothing by the Filter, is bit-identical with the Filter on or off, and can never gleam, glide, tick-lie or go stale. The **reading register** is exactly six node families: `suit.o2`, `suit.reserve`, `suit.integrity`, `suit.warmth`, `suit.charge` and the scanner reading slot. Only their glass, needle, fill and numeral pixels are lie-capable. **Stated exceptions, both in the mark slots** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the mark slots are not a seventh reading family but a **visibility exception**. (1) A suit-rung mark slot's *visibility* (never its sprite or clock, which are frame) inherits the class of the reading it sits beside (HS-30): at MVP it is driven by the Suit's rungs and is honest; at Vertical Slice A it may take the Filter's mark field for a lying reading (class R by inheritance). (2) The one-bit ship-alarm mark `suit.alarm` (HS-25, accepted at MVP by user ruling D89) is Filter-fed but its lie stage is pinned `never`, so it sits in a mark slot as a TRUTH READING (class T, Visual/Audio Requirements), neither frame nor lie-capable. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The Filter-immunity lint (AC-HS-42, AC-HS-88) therefore has an **allow-list of exactly the mark-slot visibility properties**; every other frame node stays fed nothing and bit-identical with the Filter on or off. A fixed dial face and its zone ticks are frame (engraving); the needle position against them is the reading. *Why.* "Meta elements are drawn in a register that never carries the gleam because they never carry a lie." Lie-capable pixels are exactly the pixels fed by `perceived(...)`, which makes the Filter-immunity lint checkable per node.
170	
171	**HS-4. One read path for readings: `perceived`.** *Rule.* The HUD obtains each of the five readings by `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), PlayerId)` every render frame and uses the returned record's `displayed_pm`, `displayed_value`, `motion_mode`, `tick_phase_ms`, `leak_amplitude_pm`, `leak_modes` and `frame_override`. 173	**HS-5. Non-reading fields come from `Suit.view(player_id)`.** *Rule.* Allowed: the per-axis rungs and `vitals_state`, `locomotion_cap`, `equipped_slot`, tool charges, `glowstick_count`, `carried_def_id`, `beam_shape`, whether the cell exists (`CELL_ENABLED`), plus `tool_in_hand`, `stowed_count`, `carried_instance` and `tool_charge`, **and the breath source `breath_src` (the Suit's enum 0 ROOM / 1 RESERVE / 2 GASP / 3 NONE; a `view()` field, not a reading)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. `breath_src` is the HUD's one input for three presentation choices, and for nothing else: which of two readings the strip's breath dial shows (HS-12), whether the source-exists hue is O2 Cyan or Graphite lit (ROOM or RESERVE: Cyan; GASP or NONE: Graphite lit; HS-20, HSV-4), and whether the reserve cell's mark slot is also eligible (HS-22). 210	| inspect card | layer 2, content by In-World Instruments | HUD supplies the frame, `Theme` and components only | Instruments | frame HUD-owned; reading Instruments' *(designed)* |
211	| reserved anchors | `crew_strip` top-left, `chat` left edge below it, `caption` plate slot, `own_identity` on the panel | nothing drawn at MVP | none | anchor (Vertical Slice B) |
212	
213	**Forbidden surfaces** (lint-banned under any setting or state): minimap, compass, objective, off-screen arrow, crew locator, room name, ship status or loop summary, weight / capacity / inventory / slots-free, health bar, damage number, hit flash, Attention / noise / light / illumination / exposure meter, sanity meter / icon / colour, horror indicator, threat bar, proximity indicator or direction to a Horror, beacon or breach glyph, vignette, screen-edge tint, toast, banner, popup, death screen (the `give_up` confirm plate of HS-42(b) is not a death screen and not a banner: it confirms the player's own input, shows no cause, count, countdown or consequence, and carries no death wording *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*), score, autosave glyph, "repaired" confirmation, a countdown to an event the HUD names (not the reserve numeral, HS-17), loading spinner, any text in Alarm Red, ring / radial / pie / wipe progress, and a UI cursor in `gameplay` (the cursor, reticle and aim-line bans have exactly one exception, the opt-in, off-by-default accessibility aim indicator of HS-52, user ruling D9 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*). **No HUD surface displays or sonifies the Attention level, tell progress, sanity stage or a Horror's proximity; the chest-lamp state and suit vitals are the player's own, never the web's** (Attention, Adaptive Audio). The HUD contains no horror indicator, threat bar, proximity indicator or direction: a Horror is shown in the world, never by a meter (Horror Entities; Pillar 3). **The HUD draws no beacon or breach glyph under reduce-flashing or any other setting** (Attention C27 and V14: the 'HUD glyph' named by 2D Lighting's LO-26 would be an Attention indicator, which the art bible forbids at ART:741; under reduce-flashing the static world mark and the audio carry the breach). The HS-25 ship-alarm mark is not that glyph and never keys on Attention's phase.

### Core Rules

Rule ids are `HS-n`. Each rule has *Rule.* (what is true), *Why.* (the decision it serves) and, where it matters, *Edge notes.* Implementation choices are marked `-> ADR`. A locked constant or formula is used by its registry name with the value its owner gives; a number tagged `[PH]` is a placeholder owned by this GDD (registered at Phase 5), with its range in Tuning Knobs; a name tagged *(unregistered)* is cited from its owner and is never given a HUD-side value. Constants and formulas defined by name here (`strip_budget`, `hud_flash_budget`, `reserve_seconds`, `mark_phase`, `o2_dial_angle`, `hud_settle_response`, `nonground_count`, `bottom_row_fit`, `anchor_snap`, `integrity_zone_ticks`, `charge_fill_and_warn`) are given their variables, ranges and worked examples in Formulas; the neighbours' formulas are cited by their owners' ids and never renamed here: Interaction D.UI-2 (the prompt show rule), Interaction D.UI-1 (`fill_px`, the bar), the registry's `lying_digit_tick_schedule` and Pipeline D.4 (`cap_px`).

The rules are grouped by surface: **A** identity, layer and reads (HS-1 to HS-10); **B** the critical strip (HS-11 to HS-15); **C** the suit panel (HS-16 to HS-21); **D** the warning mark (HS-22 to HS-25); **E** the lie slots (HS-26 to HS-31); **F** the hand rail (HS-32 to HS-36); **G** the prompt plate and channel bar (HS-37 to HS-45); **H** meta notices, the flash arbiter, settings, reservations, layout invariants and neighbours (HS-46 to HS-57).

#### A. Identity, layer and reads

**HS-1. The HUD draws; it decides nothing.** *Rule.* The HUD is a `PRESENTATION` subscriber of the kernel's subscriber classes. It owns no block, hook, command, mutator, reading key, RNG stream or `INPUT_SURFACE`, and "the HUD's prompts do not [issue commands]". It writes only `CanvasItem`, `Material` and audio-request properties, never a block, command, camera or viewport property. Every *when* — a rung and its hold, `prompt_state`, `length_class`, the tick schedule, the lie stage, the save-failure count, alarm eligibility — is cited from its owner and never derived by the HUD. *Why.* The scope guard: the HUD is the scene-tree side of the kernel's rule that simulation systems stay scene-tree free. *Edge notes.* If a needed *when* has no owner (the ship-alarm source; the warmth band edges had no owner until SE-29 published them), the HUD raises an ASK (Open Questions) and draws nothing in the interim; it never invents the rule.

**HS-2. Layer 2, in the root viewport.** *Rule.* The HUD is a `CanvasLayer` (layer 2, group `hud`) in the **root viewport**, never inside the 640 x 360 world `SubViewport`. It receives no world light, glow, ambient, occlusion, Filter pass, camera shake or jolt, by construction (a different viewport). The HUD scale `H` is an integer in `{H_default .. 2 * H_default}` (and, at MVP, in the `offered(P_w, P_h)` subset of it, D.8) with `H_default = max(k_auto, 3)` (`HUD_MIN_SCALE` 3; the Pipeline's PR-12 form: `k_auto` is the picture's automatic world scale, not the live zoom step `k`), independent of the world scale `k` and of the zoom ladder (`k` in `[1, k_auto + 2]`); *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* a zoom step or an `H` change alters no simulation value. No HUD code reads `k` or assumes `H == k`: its only scale inputs are `H` and the picture rect. *Why.* P1: the frame is an anchor. The Pipeline's two-integer-scales-in-one-window wiring (the Steam Deck: world 2x, HUD 3x) is an MVP requirement whose wiring is NOT SOURCEABLE until the Pipeline's spike step 11. *Edge notes.* A `Control` found under the world `SubViewport` fails the scene-tree lint (Pipeline lint (b)); in a release build it would receive world light and the Filter, so this is a build gate, not a runtime check.

**HS-3. Frame register versus reading register.** *Rule.* Screen space has two registers. The **frame register** — plates, bezels, chamfers, rivets, keycaps, labels, the prompt plate, the bar, the rail glyphs and counts, the failed-write notice, the first-frame line, the focus bracket — is fed nothing by the Filter, is bit-identical with the Filter on or off, and can never gleam, glide, tick-lie or go stale. The **reading register** is exactly six node families: `suit.o2`, `suit.reserve`, `suit.integrity`, `suit.warmth`, `suit.charge` and the scanner reading slot. Only their glass, needle, fill and numeral pixels are lie-capable. **Stated exceptions, both in the mark slots** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the mark slots are not a seventh reading family but a **visibility exception**. (1) A suit-rung mark slot's *visibility* (never its sprite or clock, which are frame) inherits the class of the reading it sits beside (HS-30): at MVP it is driven by the Suit's rungs and is honest; at Vertical Slice A it may take the Filter's mark field for a lying reading (class R by inheritance). (2) The one-bit ship-alarm mark `suit.alarm` (HS-25, accepted at MVP by user ruling D89) is Filter-fed but its lie stage is pinned `never`, so it sits in a mark slot as a TRUTH READING (class T, Visual/Audio Requirements), neither frame nor lie-capable. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The Filter-immunity lint (AC-HS-42, AC-HS-88) therefore has an **allow-list of exactly the mark-slot visibility properties**; every other frame node stays fed nothing and bit-identical with the Filter on or off. A fixed dial face and its zone ticks are frame (engraving); the needle position against them is the reading. *Why.* "Meta elements are drawn in a register that never carries the gleam because they never carry a lie." Lie-capable pixels are exactly the pixels fed by `perceived(...)`, which makes the Filter-immunity lint checkable per node.

**HS-4. One read path for readings: `perceived`.** *Rule.* The HUD obtains each of the five readings by `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), PlayerId)` every render frame and uses the returned record's `displayed_pm`, `displayed_value`, `motion_mode`, `tick_phase_ms`, `leak_amplitude_pm`, `leak_modes` and `frame_override`. It **never calls `true_value`**: HUD modules hold zero `true_value` call sites (the Filter's AC-PF-51). A `Perceived` record is never cached across frames; the per-frame `HudModel` holds values *copied this frame* and overwritten every frame, which is a model, not a cache of records. **The read fills a reusable, caller-owned record** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the HUD passes one preallocated `Perceived` struct per reading to the Filter's read (`perceived(key, viewer, out)`), so steady state allocates nothing per frame (a fresh record per reading per frame would allocate in GDScript every render frame, AC-HS-92); "never cached" still means no value is held for reuse after the frame's draw. This is an ask to the Filter (its read signature). *The Suit's and the Filter's "must repeat" clauses, restated with the correction:* the O2 numeral is the suit's `p_o2` reading; every HR-3 reading reaches the HUD only through `perceived`, which wraps the Suit's `true_value(key, player_id)` for `suit.o2`, `suit.reserve`, `suit.integrity`, `suit.warmth` and `suit.charge`; no reading is corrupted in the MVP; and the Filter may neither remove nor add a body cue, move the chest point, or edit overlay visibility. *Why.* The registry entry `perceived_query` says the Filter is the only non-diagnostic caller of the Graph's `true_value(kind, id)` and of the Suit's `true_value(key, player_id)`. This GDD adopts that wording; the Suit's SE-29 clause "reach the HUD only through `true_value`" is the stale one (refresh owed, Cross-References). *Edge notes.* A missing record (a key not yet registered) draws the reading's plate with a blank numeral and the arc at rest, counts `HUD_READ_MISSING`, and never falls back to `view()`.

**HS-5. Non-reading fields come from `Suit.view(player_id)`.** *Rule.* Allowed: the per-axis rungs and `vitals_state`, `locomotion_cap`, `equipped_slot`, tool charges, `glowstick_count`, `carried_def_id`, `beam_shape`, whether the cell exists (`CELL_ENABLED`), plus `tool_in_hand`, `stowed_count`, `carried_instance` and `tool_charge`, **and the breath source `breath_src` (the Suit's enum 0 ROOM / 1 RESERVE / 2 GASP / 3 NONE; a `view()` field, not a reading)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. `breath_src` is the HUD's one input for three presentation choices, and for nothing else: which of two readings the strip's breath dial shows (HS-12), whether the source-exists hue is O2 Cyan or Graphite lit (ROOM or RESERVE: Cyan; GASP or NONE: Graphite lit; HS-20, HSV-4), and whether the reserve cell's mark slot is also eligible (HS-22). It is a published enum, so the hue and the dial choice are frame-register decisions (class A, bit-identical with the Filter on or off, AC-HS-139) and not a corruptible reading; the HUD never derives a source from a `displayed_*` value. The four pre-wrap reading fields of `view()` (`o2_pp_dkpa`, `reserve_pm`, `cell_pm`, `integrity_pm`) are **never drawn**: a HUD that draws a number from them is a defect (the Suit's lint AC-SE-77). *Why.* A number drawn from `view()` would bypass the single wrap point (P4). *Edge notes.* In tests only, `view()` reading fields may be compared against the drawn value on the honest path (the second-instrument assertion, HS-14).

**HS-6. The read interface is closed.** *Rule.* The HUD's reads are exactly those in the table below; anything else is a scope breach.

| Read | Owner | Fields the HUD uses | Frequency | Never read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), PlayerId)` x 5, plus the one-bit `perceived(SUIT_KEY(suit.alarm), PlayerId)` for the ship-alarm mark (a TRUTH key with its lie stage pinned `never`; how the one bit sits in the record is the Filter's, OQ-HS-8; **the Filter does not yet define the key, OQ-HS-79, so this read is provisional**) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | Perception Filter | the record fields of HS-4 | every render frame | the true value, the lie id or kind as content |
| `perceived(SCANNER, PlayerId)` *(MVP-live and honest: Sanity SN-19, Interaction IA-30; only what a scan shows is provisional — ASK Sanity / Interaction)* | Perception Filter | same record | while the scanner slot is shown | — |
| `Suit.view(PlayerId)` + `tool_in_hand`, `stowed_count`, `carried_instance`, `tool_charge` | Suit & Equipment | HS-5 list | discrete part: on dirty key `S/<PlayerId>`; forced rebuild list in HS-7 | the four reading fields |
| `focus_view(seat)` | Interaction | `focus_ref`, `anchor_o`, `verb_id`, `mode`, `duration_class`, `tool_required`, `prompt_state`, `verb_name_key`, `glyph_action`, `focus_seq`, and the fields Interaction's design review added (IA-41): `press_blocked_moving` (true only on CHANNEL and HOLD_CONFIRM plates; the HUD draws the keycap hollow with the verb text Paper White and never hides the plate; Interaction IA-41 as amended in its re-review, AC-IA-142) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; CD ruling on PCI re-review)*, `carry_state`, `drop_available`, `drop_anchor_o` (the second drop plate, HS-43; drawing details are the UX spec's) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, `self_target` (bool, Interaction IA-41: true when the focus is the actor's own suit, the Controller's PC-6 self-target; selects the self plate of HS-37 / HS-39, which has no `anchor_o`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP)* | every render frame | `interaction.state`, `node()`, `edge()`, any `PERCEPTION_OUT` block |
| `channel_view(seat)` (local seat only) | Interaction | `owner`, `verb_id`, `state`, `transition_seq`, `result_seq`, `progress_pm`, `length_class`, `outcome`, `ended_by` | every render frame | `abort_cause` (Interaction IA-41: "diagnostic only"; the cancel drain is keyed off the non-diagnostic `ended_by` instead, HS-41) |
| `confirm_view(seat)` *(the HUD's single named read for the hold and the press; the Controller publishes it as `confirm_view = {b, pressed, released}`, pci:953, and Interaction IA-41 names the same read `input_view(seat) = {hold_pm, armed, device_class, pressed_action}`, owned by the Controller; **the two names and field sets must be reconciled by the Controller (OQ-HS-18)**, this GDD uses `confirm_view` and the union below)* | Player Controller (Adapter-local, per render frame) | `{mode, hold_pm, armed, pressed_action, released, give_up_live}`: `mode` the Controller's `confirm_mode` (`HOLD` or `TAP`, pci:552 / 882); `hold_pm` 0..1000, the D.10 bar fill `b` as permille (the Controller drains it itself at `CONFIRM_DRAIN_RATE`; the HUD draws it, `fill_px = (hold_pm * L) div 1000`, and does no drain of its own for a hold); `armed` the tap-confirm armed state; `pressed_action` the closed action token whose press is being acknowledged, or none; `released` true on the frame a held action is released. The Controller's published shape lacked `mode` and `armed` (Interaction's lacks `mode` and `released`): an ASK to add them (OQ-HS-18), **met on the Controller's side 2026-10-28** (PCI UI Requirements 1 now publishes `{b, mode, armed, pressed, released, give_up_live}`); the remaining reconciliation is the field names (`b` / `hold_pm`, `pressed` / `pressed_action`) and the single read name, OQ-HS-18 (1) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. **The HUD's TAP-mode relabel and armed-bracket story (HS-42) depends on the Controller story that lands those fields** (no longer blocked at design level); the ACK, hold-fill and glyph-swap stories depend only on the fields already published (`b`, `pressed`, `released`, `device`, `token`) and are not blocked. **`give_up_live`** bool: the Controller's "`loco_state == DOWNED` in solo, context `gameplay`, and no other bound seat could revive the actor (Co-op Session's gating)"; it is the HUD's only trigger for the `give_up` confirm plate (HS-42(b)); `pressed_action` may be `give_up`; the HUD never reads `loco_state` itself. ASK to the Controller: publish `give_up_live` in `confirm_view` (PCI UI Requirements 1, which as amended 2026-10-28 publishes `{b, mode, armed, pressed, released, give_up_live}`) and add it to the registry entry's `input_view` values (OQ-HS-18). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; CD ruling on PCI re-review)* | every render frame while a hold, a tap-arm or a press is live, and every render frame while `give_up_live` is true | `loco_state` |
| `glyph_view(seat, action)` *(agreed in shape: pci:953)* | Player Controller (Adapter) | `{device, token}`: `device` in {KBM, PAD}, switched under `DEVICE_SWITCH_HYSTERESIS`; `token` from the Controller's **closed `keycap_token` enumeration** (one token per key, mouse button and gamepad button or axis direction its binding table can hold; a binding outside it fails the Controller's data-load lint). The `?` keycap (HS-37) is the HUD's fallback only for a token its own **atlas** lacks, never a member of the Controller's enumeration. The closed action set includes `give_up` (Backspace / View) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | on device switch | `InputEvent.device`, any comparison to `0` |
| The result-event record *(Interaction IA-41 source 4; agreed in shape)* | Interaction / kernel CR-5 projection | `{seat, command_id, queued_tick, kind}` with `kind` in {APPLIED, REJECTED, DROPPED, SUPERSEDED}, for the local seat's own commands only, carrying **no reason**; used to withdraw an ACK and to time the reject presentation | on each result | the reject reason |
| `save_status`, the fallback-load flag, `restore_reason` (a request only) | Save/Load | `IDLE / WRITING / WRITTEN / FAILED`; the consecutive-failure threshold is cited, not counted | on change | the failure count's meaning beyond the threshold |
| Committed tick `T`, `tick_alpha`, `present_time`, picture rect, `H`, `world_to_hud(pos)` | Kernel, Render Pipeline | as named | every render frame | the jolt offset; the world camera pose directly |
| O2 band edges | Life-Support Graph | `O2_BAND_ANOXIC_PP`, `HYPOXIA_PP`, `O2_BAND_THIN_PP` (registry; HS-13) | at load | any compartment state, `failures()`, `alarm_eligible` |

The HUD never reads Attention, Horror, Sanity state, the Graph's state at a distance, `peer_id`, `lit(ref)` or the beam's exposure; `prompt_state` already carries what Interaction decided about lighting. It does not read the Controller's `input_ignored_view(seat)`: that read is refused (K43). The only visual response to an ignored or rejected press is the MOVING tell above (the presser's own state) and HS-41's reject keycap hold on a plate Interaction has already shown; a press at a HIDDEN-prompt (unlit) subject draws nothing (P3, AC-HS-143). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; CD ruling on PCI re-review)* *Why.* Reflexion pattern 11: list only what the consumer must supply, never a producer's internals; Graph UI item 4 forbids ship status at a distance; P3.

**HS-7. Update model: hybrid pull.** *Rule.* Each render frame the HUD pulls the five `perceived` records, `focus_view(seat)`, `channel_view(seat)` and the Adapter reads of HS-6 (they can change every frame: glide, re-projection, bar). The seat's dirty key `S/<PlayerId>` and `save_status` changes decide only whether the **discrete** model (rungs, `vitals_state`, rail counts, `equipped_slot`, `carried_def_id`, the notice) is rebuilt. A rebuild is **forced** regardless of the key on: the first `RUNNING` frame, any restore, an `ALL`-coalesced notification (above `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256), exit from `PAUSED`, and any change of `H`, locale or glyph device. Notifications carry no state. *Why.* A coalesced `ALL` must not strand a stale reading; readings can glide so they must be pulled; the discrete rebuild is a dozen integer reads so the skip is a convenience, not a correctness dependency. -> ADR candidate C.

**HS-8. Clocks.** *Rule.* Reading settle, prompt debounce, bar fill, bar drain, tick phases and lie motion advance on `present_time`, which is frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED`. The warning-mark phase is read from the committed kernel tick `T` and interpolated by `tick_alpha` (HS-23), **and so are the honest-numeral grid (`T mod HONEST_GRID_TICKS == 0`, HS-14) and the flash arbiter's window (`(T - TICK_RATE, T]`, HS-47)**, which freeze with `T` under pause; while `PAUSED` an active mark is held ON solid instead (HS-23), the one exception to the frozen-frame rule. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the grid moved from `present_time` to `T` so it cannot drift against the mark's own `T`-locked edges)* Layer 3 (the Chart Table) runs on process time. A time step fed to any presentation timer after a pause, a window-focus loss or a hitch is clamped (`HUD_DT_CLAMP_MS` 50 `[PH]`), and no integrator divides by the time step. *Why.* The art bible 7.4 "the world simply stops"; the Pipeline's own state table says "HUD visible (frozen readings); chart table live on process time". The Pipeline's PR-9 prose "Layers 2-4 run on the engine's process time" is the stale clause (refresh owed: "Layers 3-4"; Cross-References). *Edge notes.* The Pipeline's PR-8 item 6 ("never on the tick counter") needs the matching wording refresh "never counts ticks; may read `T` and `tick_alpha` for clock-locked phases". -> ADR candidate B.

**HS-9. Integer HUD-pixel placement and primitives, at every `H` and display.** *Rule (observable).* Every element is authored in HUD px (1 HUD px = `H` screen px), anchored to an edge or the centre of the HUD canvas `picture / H` (which may be fractional: the Deck's 1280 x 800 picture at `H` 3 is 426.67 wide), and snapped by `anchor_snap` so that every edge lands on a whole HUD px. Sizes are exact integer multiples of `H`. **Coordinate space (design review, 2026-10-27):** `HudLayout` outputs **integer HUD-px rectangles relative to the HUD-root `Control`** that the pipeline root sizes to `hud_rect / H` on every `RESCALING` (Pipeline PR-12, as amended; `world_to_hud` returns coordinates in the same space). The scale `H`, the sub-`H` screen-pixel remainder (`extra_x`) and any letterbox offset are carried by that Control's placement and the `CanvasLayer` transform, not by `HudLayout`; D.9's screen-pixel terms are the conversion a test uses, not a second layout space. **The default is manual snapping in `HudLayout`** (floor every rectangle to a whole HUD px and split the remainder as D.9 says); `gui_snap_controls_to_pixels` is neither sourced nor relied on, and spikes S1 and S4 are **prerequisites of the layout / widget ADR**, not non-gating (the property, if it works, is a bonus). Layout and settings changes (`H`, locale, picture rect, `k_auto`) take effect on the **next render frame in every state, including `PAUSED_FROZEN`** (the layout is a pure function of `(picture rect, H)`; no simulation or presentation timer is advanced by it). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `Control.scale` is (1, 1) everywhere; no node animates scale or rotation; the 4.7 `Control.offset_transform_*` properties are not used for settle. Bars, strokes and dial arcs are filled rectangles or atlas regions on the art-pixel grid, not `draw_line` or `draw_arc` primitives, because 4.7 line drawing has no antialiasing feather. A needle's tip is quantised to whole HUD px, and the Filter's never-rest rule (`NEVER_REST_MAX_S` 1.0 s) must hold at that quantisation. `gui_snap_controls_to_pixels` **is set to true on the root only as a bonus if spike S1 shows it exists and takes effect on the HUD `CanvasLayer`; nothing relies on it, and no criterion asserts a HUD-px position through it** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the rule had said both "not relied on" and "= true on the root")*: the property is the Pipeline's (K21), is **NOT SOURCEABLE** in the pinned reference, and its scope is `[UNV]` (it may be viewport- or project-scoped and so may not apply to a `CanvasLayer`'s controls at all; it appears nowhere under `docs/engine-reference/godot/`; what is sourced is the 4.7 line no-feather rule, breaking-changes.md:31 and rendering.md:11, and `offset_transform` in ui.md). *Why.* HR-6 and the Pipeline's rule that human-built geometry including the HUD is never rotated at runtime (PR-4 rule 5, which lists the HUD). *Edge notes.* How a needle is produced (a pre-baked frame strip, a snapped sprite, a polygon) is -> ADR candidate A; the observable requirement is only the quantisation and the never-rest proof. Behaviour of `gui_snap_controls_to_pixels` when `H != k` and with a fractional canvas is NOT SOURCEABLE until the spike.

**HS-10. The surface inventory is closed.** *Rule.* The HUD has exactly the surfaces in the table below. Anything else is a scope breach and a lint failure.

| Surface | Anchor | Contents | Source read | Register |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hud_strip` | centre-bottom, sitting on the bottom 5 % safe margin | the **breath dial**: arc with pivot cap, three-cell numeral, mark slot; it shows the ambient O2 while `breath_src` is ROOM, GASP or NONE and the suit O2 (the reserve) while it is RESERVE (HS-12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | `perceived(suit.o2)` in ROOM, GASP and NONE; `perceived(suit.reserve)` in RESERVE; `view` rung and `breath_src` | reading |
| `hud_suit_panel` | bottom-left, inside the margin | reserve, integrity, warmth, charge + lamp switch; per-reading mark slots; the ship-alarm mark slot (HS-22, HS-25); the **ambient-O2 slot** (a three-digit numeral field in the reserve cell, lit only while the strip shows the reserve, HS-12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; notice slot; reserved `own_identity` slot *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | `perceived` x 4 + `suit.alarm`, `view` | reading (glass, needle, numeral, fill) + frame |
| `hud_rail` | bottom-right, inside the margin | three tool slots in a four-slot geometry (the fourth cell reserved and empty at MVP, X6), glowstick count, carried glyph, scanner reading slot, device keycaps *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | `view`, `tool_*`, glyph token read, `perceived(SCANNER)` | frame + one reading slot |
| `hud_prompt` and `hud_bar` | `world_to_hud(anchor_o)` of the focused subject; the self-plate variant is placed per HS-39's self-plate rule (outside the chest keep-out, no world anchor) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP)* | plate (keycap + verb), NEEDS_TOOL variant, self-plate variant (HS-37; `verb_patch_self`), the linear bar (riding on whichever plate is drawn) | `focus_view` (including `self_target`, which feeds the self-plate variant), `channel_view`, hold state | frame (meta) |

content.content: 245	**HS-23. One alarm rhythm.** *Rule.* The mark phase is `mark_phase = ((T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS) + tick_alpha) / BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS`, with `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` 128 (2.133 s); the mark is ON while the phase is below `MARK_DUTY_PM / 1000` with `MARK_DUTY_PM` 500 `[PH]` (range 400-600). `MARK_PERIOD_TICKS` is `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` **by relation, never a second value**. The leading edge falls at `T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS == 0`, the same grid as the beacon sweep and the annunciator (Adaptive Audio's AAV-9). There are no per-mark offsets and no per-mark epoch: all marks share one phase, with or without a beacon in scope (the fallback epoch `(T - breach_enter_T)` is Audio's branch for a listener without a beacon, cited, not re-owned). The mark is drawn on the first render frame whose `(T, tick_alpha)` is at or past a boundary (at most one render frame of skew against the audio edge: 16.7 ms at 60 fps). Under reduced motion or reduce-flashing the mark holds ON solid and the sound carries the alarm. **At the first-launch default the mark is therefore solid:** `reduce_flashing` defaults ON (user ruling D79), so the beacon-phase pulse, the 64-tick appearance latency and the pause-bridge arithmetic below apply to a player who has turned reduce flashing off and kept reduced motion off, and the sound carries the alarm by default (note to Adaptive Audio, AAV-19; OQ-HS-76) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **While the kernel is `PAUSED` (solo pause, `PAUSED_FROZEN`) any mark that is active is held ON solid, with no edges: the same rule reduced motion already uses.** `T` does not advance under pause, so no mark can appear or clear during it; an inactive slot stays empty; the phase is not consulted while paused and resumes from the unchanged `T` on the first `RUNNING` frame, the mark bridged ON until the next leading edge (below). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* This is **the one stated exception to "last frame held"** (HS-53, States and Transitions), adopted at CD-GDD-ALIGN (stage 12) on the art-director's alternative. *Why.* "One rhythm for alarm everywhere" and P1/P2: a pause that froze the mark in its OFF outline beside a CRITICAL reading would make the honest frame register look safe when it is not, and the player would return from pause with no alarm showing. Holding ON keeps the alarm legible for as long as the world is stopped, at the cost of one element's departure from the frozen-frame rule. *Edge notes.* **Flash arithmetic** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: entering the hold from an OFF phase is one mark leading edge, and leaving it on resume (when the unchanged `T` is in an OFF phase) would be a trailing edge; both are mark edges in the arbiter (HS-47: never deferred, never delayed), so one pause cycle would cost one leading edge and one trailing edge. **Resume bridge (the HUD-side dwell guard, design review 2026-10-27):** on resume the mark does not leave the held-ON state until the **next leading edge** (`T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS == 0`), after which it follows the phase again; the one OFF stretch it skips is the price. Result: a pause entered in an OFF phase costs one leading edge, a resume costs none, and a pause re-entered before that next leading edge finds the mark already ON and costs none, so toggling pause cannot drive the mark past the ceiling whatever the Chart Table does. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* No numeral grid boundary, prompt show-start or Filter tick occurs while paused (`present_time` is frozen), so a pause adds no other event. Under reduced motion or reduce-flashing the mark is already solid and a pause adds no edge at all. Pause re-toggle spam is bounded by the HUD's resume bridge above (AC-HS-133); the Chart Table's minimum re-toggle interval (OQ-HS-62) stays a recommended second guard, no longer the only one. Status: the creative-director's recommendation, still subject to user confirmation (OQ-HS-4).

314	**HS-46. The failed-write notice and the first-frame line.** *Rule.* **Notice:** a 16 x 16 Paper White "record slot" glyph on a chamfered Ground plate at the suit panel's edge, with the one phrase (string key `notice_save_failed`, English placeholder "The game could not write its record.") in the reading face, shown only while Save/Load reports the failed-write escalation: `save_status` reads `FAILED` on every failed write (sl:739), and the notice is raised only after `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_ESCALATE_COUNT` (registry: 3, range 1-10, Save/Load) consecutive failures (sl:739, sl:1006). **The HUD counts nothing**: it reads a Save/Load-published escalation flag (`fail_escalated`, bool, a Save/Load SL-21 host-local read, registry `save_status` companion_read; true from the 3rd consecutive failed write until the next `WRITTEN`); persistent, non-modal, no animation, no cause, cleared by the next `WRITTEN`; no Alarm Red, no Flesh, no Violet; never lie-capable. There is **no per-write glyph**: UI-1 is retired, `STATUS_WRITTEN_HOLD_TICKS` stays retired, and no sound, text or mark announces an autosave. **First-frame line (UI-7):** one plain reading-face line ("Newest record unreadable. Continuing from the one before it.", placeholder) on a Ground plate stacked at the panel's edge above the notice slot, on the first `RUNNING` frame after a fallback load, for `UI7_DWELL_S` 8 `[PH]` (range 5-15) and then a cut; if the Chart Table already shows it under Continue, the HUD shows nothing. **Second trigger, `DEATH_STUB` (user ruling D15 / D84):** on the first `RUNNING` frame after a restore whose `restore_reason` is `DEATH_STUB`, the same slot shows one plain ship-log line (string key `line_record_restored`, English placeholder "Restored from the last record."; no death wording, no cause, no count, no summary of what was lost) for `UI7_DWELL_S`, then a cut. The Chart Table shows nothing at a death restore (the restore is in-game and automatic, SL-7), so the HUD always shows it. **Both at once:** if the fallback flag is also set, the fallback line is shown and the death line is not (the fallback line already says the game is continuing from an earlier record; one line at a time, no queue). `restore_reason` stays a request: it keys this one line and alters nothing else (HS-53) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. (orchestrator ruling: the ui-programmer's "centre-low" placement is dropped; both meta plates share the panel's edge so nothing new enters the bottom-centre band.) *Why.* Save/Load's UI-10 and UI-7; the Chart Table's ASK-CT-5 agrees.
315	
316	**HS-47. The flash arbiter (`hud_flash_budget`).** *Rule.* One arbiter counts luminance events per rolling second across the HUD. **Its clock is the committed tick `T`** (window `(T - TICK_RATE, T]`): `present_time` drives animation, not the budget; an event that originates in render time (a focus becoming stable, a press) is stamped with the tick current at that render frame, and while the kernel is `PAUSED` `T` does not advance, so no deferrable event is admitted while paused. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The event inventory** (every HUD luminance event, with its class; the events added by the review are marked *new*): **clock-locked, never delayed:** mark leading edges (at `T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS == 0`); honest-numeral **grid boundaries** at `T mod HONEST_GRID_TICKS == 0` at which at least one displayed digit actually changes (a boundary with no displayed change is not an event, so the 2 events/s is a ceiling reached only while the numerals are falling), which are **skip-only**: drawn on their own tick or skipped, never delayed. **Never rescheduled by the HUD:** lying-digit ticks (the Filter's schedule). **Follow the honest source state, counted, never deferred:** source-state hue cuts (HSV-4, L-5: a glyph or arc band changing between its loop hue and Graphite lit). **Source-state swap** *(new, re-review)*: the strip's `breath_src` swap (HS-12, HSV-42), counted once, never deferred, like a hue cut. **give_up plate show-start and hide** (HS-42(b), HSV-43) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: they follow `confirm_view.give_up_live`; the show is never deferred (it must appear on the first DOWNED frame), a hide is immediate and counts under the orphan rule if its show lies before the window; re-shows are spaced by `since_last_show >= PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS` (EC-HS-57), so the plate contributes at most 3 show-starts per second; in WEIGHTED mode the show-start is treated as a prompt show-start for the `flash_weight_pm` exemption (neither counted nor deferred below `FLASH_AREA_EXEMPT_PM`), in STRICT it is counted and may overrun (`HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN` recorded, nothing dropped). **Orphan transitions** *(new, re-review)*: a plate hide whose show-start lies before the window, and a mark OFF edge whose ON edge does, are counted once in `N(w)` for the windows that contain them (they are known only when they occur, so they are non-deferrable and may overrun, D.2). **A counted mark event is an actual change in the drawn luminance of a mark slot, not a scheduled boundary** *(new, re-review)*: three cases were missing from the inventory. (1) A **leading edge** at `T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS == 0` counts only when the slot is active and was drawn OFF (outline to fill); at a tick where the mark is already drawn ON (held solid by STRICT or reduced motion, held by pause, or bridged after a resume, HS-23) the natural edge changes nothing and is **not** counted. (2) A **mid-phase appearance**: an inactive slot becoming active draws the filled square at once when it is solid (STRICT, reduced motion) or when the live phase is inside the duty (D.4), which is one counted, non-deferrable event at that tick; in the pulsing case outside the duty it draws the OFF outline (a luminance change, one event) and the next leading edge is then counted normally. (3) The **pause-induced edge** (entering the hold from an OFF phase) is one event, per HS-23. The scheduled mark entry in `W(t)` is conditional: it exists only for a slot that is active **and** pulsing (not solid, not paused), so a solid mark reserves no capacity. **Input-driven, two classes** *(re-review: the earlier single class, "counted, never deferred", let spam raise the HUD above the ceiling and is replaced)*: **(A) State displays**, whose *simulation state changes at once and is never delayed* but whose *drawn state* goes through **one shared coalescing limiter** for the whole class: the tool-switch bracket and Tungsten move (HSV-13), the glowstick count substitution (HSV-15; the suppressant's, HSV-14, is dormant until the tool returns), the lamp-switch glyph (HS-19, HSV-12), and the TAP-mode "Confirm?" relabel and its disarm or expiry restore (HS-42, *new to the inventory*), the give_up plate's TAP relabel and bracket (HS-42(b)), and the hollow-keycap tell of `press_blocked_moving` on and off (HS-6; admitted through the one limiter, latest state always shown) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The limiter admits at most one state-display draw per `GLYPH_STATE_LATCH_TICKS` 20 across the **whole class** (so at most 3 per rolling second from the class, not 3 per kind), each admitted draw shows the **latest** simulation state (intermediate states are never drawn, the count and the bracket jump straight to the current value), and each admitted draw is also a deferrable event through `admit` (so it yields to prompts and the grid and never lands in a full window); a pending draw that has waited `MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 60 is force-admitted and counted (overrun, recorded). The final drawn state therefore equals the simulation state within `MAX_DEFER_TICKS` ticks of the last change (AC-HS-140). **(B) Acknowledgement cues**, which cannot be deferred without a press feeling unreceived (Game Feel step 2, the same render frame as the accepted press): the force-admitted show-start of an accepted press and the ACK keycap dip (one event, they land on the same frame, HS-37, HSV-24), the reject keycap hold (HS-41), the keycap dip on a `give_up` press (ACK, one event, rate-gated to one per `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS` per seat, HS-42(b)) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, and the OUTCOME plate-border step (HSV-29), which follows the simulation's result. They are counted and never deferred, **rate-gated by their own gates** (at most one ACK-plus-force-admit and at most one reject presentation per seat per `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS`; one OUTCOME step per channel), and **may overrun a full window**: an overrun is recorded as `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN` and nothing is dropped. **Deferrable:** prompt show-starts with no press; the scanner reading's show-start (HSV-34, *new*); the notice and first-frame-line show-starts; and the state-display class (A) as above (lowest priority). Positional changes (bar fill, needle motion, arc settle, charge-fill steps) are not luminance events. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Two counting modes (user rulings D91 (iv) and D79)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: `flash_mode` is STRICT while `reduce_flashing` is on (its first-launch default) and WEIGHTED otherwise. STRICT counts every event of the inventory above, as before. WEIGHTED weights a flash by the area it changes (WCAG 2.3.1; the registry's `flash_count` takes a region as a ninth of the displayed picture) and exempts exactly two classes, **honest-numeral digit swaps (grid boundaries) and prompt show-starts**, when the event's `flash_weight_pm` is below `FLASH_AREA_EXEMPT_PM` (D.2). An exempt event is neither counted nor deferred, so a prompt waits for its debounce alone; the grid stays clock-locked and skip-only in both modes because it is a shared cadence, not a budget decision. **The Alarm Red mark's edges are always counted strictly, in both modes** (a red flash is held to the strict ceiling; `flash_count` includes red flash). Every other event of the inventory (source-state hue cuts, input-driven small-area events, notice, scanner and lamp-glyph changes) stays counted in both modes. Lying-digit ticks are the Filter's schedule and are counted in both modes until the Filter adopts the same weighting (note to the Perception Filter). A deferrable event is admitted at tick `t` only if the count in the half-open window `(t - TICK_RATE, t]` plus itself plus the clock-locked events already scheduled in that window stays at or below `FLASH_MAX_PER_S`; otherwise it waits. The normative admission test is the Formulas entry D.2 (`hud_flash_budget`), which also checks every forward window ending at an already-scheduled clock-locked event in `(t, t + TICK_RATE)`; this sentence is its summary. Hide events are never deferred. **Priority order (HUD-owned; it never touches the Filter's scheduler; in WEIGHTED mode the exempt classes leave the order and it governs what remains):** hides are never deferred; mark edges are never deferred; Filter lying-digit ticks are never rescheduled; among the HUD-owned deferrable events (the grid boundary is skip-only, never delayed) the order is prompt show-start, then the honest grid boundary, then notice or scanner show-start, then the state-display class (the lamp-switch glyph, the bracket, the count, the TAP relabel). **Grid-skip rule, with its bounds** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: a grid boundary that would exceed the budget while a prompt show-start waits is skipped, and the next boundary shows the then-latest value; **a boundary is never skipped twice in a row** (`GRID_MAX_CONSEC_SKIPS` 1, a rule constant, not a knob): the boundary after a skip is admitted and counted whatever waits, so **numeral lag is bounded by `2 x HONEST_TICK_MS` unconditionally**. 338	### States and Transitions
339	
340	The HUD has no simulation state. Its states are **presentation states** that follow the Pipeline's state (`PAUSED_FROZEN`, `TRANSIT_HOLD`) and the local seat's life state, plus a few presentation-local latches. No HUD state is ever written to the simulation, saved, replicated or hashed; on a restore every presentation-local counter is cleared (HS-53).
341	
342	#### Surface-level states
343	
344	| State | Entry | Exit | HUD behaviour | Who may cause the transition |
345	|---|---|---|---|---|
346	| **UNMOUNTED** | Boot, or the front-end (Chart Table main menu) with no world loaded | The world scene is live and the first committed tick exists | Nothing drawn; no model; no read of `view()` before the first commit (draw the last committed state; none means nothing) | Pipeline / boot flow |
347	| **RESTORE_FRAME** (one render frame) | The first `RUNNING` frame after any load or restore | The next render frame | Readings drawn directly at the restored values (needle at the restored fraction, numerals set directly, the hold grid armed from that frame); **no settle, no abort frame, no break-notch**; debounce counters, bar fill and drain, tick phases, flash history and the device latch are cleared; the first-frame line (HS-46: after a fallback load or a `DEATH_STUB` restore) may start; the mark phase comes from the live `T` with no start artefact; `restore_reason` is read only as a request and never alters hallucination content from `DEATH_STUB` (it keys only the one record line) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | Save/Load (a restore), kernel boot |
348	| **RUNNING** | RESTORE_FRAME done | `PAUSED`, `TRANSIT_HOLD`, DOWNED, DEAD | Full behaviour: readings pulled every frame, prompt and bar live, mark on the beacon grid | Kernel |
349	| **PAUSED_FROZEN** (solo pause) | The kernel is `PAUSED` | Resume | The last frame is held (one exception, below), **not dimmed, blurred or desaturated**; readings frozen (`present_time` and `T` stop); **an active mark is held ON solid, the one stated exception to "last frame held" (HS-23)**; the prompt and bar freeze; layer 3 (Chart Table) is live on process time over the HUD; on exit a forced discrete rebuild (HS-7) and a clamped time step (HS-8), and the mark stays ON until the next leading edge (the resume bridge, HS-23) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Kernel pause; Chart Table |
350	| **OVERLAY** (co-op pause, Vertical Slice B) | A co-op overlay opens with the kernel RUNNING | The overlay closes | The HUD runs normally; the bottom-right rail may be covered by the opaque overlay panel; no HUD rule depends on rail visibility (HS-36) | Chart Table / Co-op Session *(provisional)* |
351	| **TRANSIT_HOLD** / pod leg | The pod hop begins | Arrival | The HUD's layout is unchanged (HR-3: layer 1 goes black, the HUD stays) but **statuses run in the pod** (user ruling D60): the readings keep updating from `perceived`, and the needle, numerals, marks and arbiter behave as in RUNNING; still lie-capable; the prompt is hidden unless a lit plate exists; a death in the pod is the Controller's DEAD (below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | Web Map & Transit, Suit, Controller |

# TRs: HUD & Suit Layer (alias: hud)

Source: design/gdd/hud-and-suit-layer.md (Presentation, MVP; systems index row 21). No ADR exists; ADR candidates A-G are listed in Overview.

| Req ID | Requirement | Domain | GDD anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| TR-hud-001 | The HUD is a `PRESENTATION`-class kernel subscriber that owns no block, hook, command, mutator, reading key, RNG stream or `INPUT_SURFACE`, and writes only CanvasItem/Material/audio-request properties. | Core | HS-1 |
| TR-hud-002 | The HUD is a `CanvasLayer` (layer 2, group `hud`) in the root viewport, never under the 640x360 world `SubViewport`; a `Control` under the world SubViewport fails the scene-tree lint (build gate). | Rendering | HS-2 |
| TR-hud-003 | HUD scale `H` is an integer in `{H_default..2*H_default}` with `H_default = max(k_auto,3)`, independent of world scale `k`; HUD code never reads `k` or assumes `H==k`; an `H` change alters no simulation value. | Rendering | HS-2, HUD_MIN_SCALE |
| TR-hud-004 | Frame-register nodes (plates, keycaps, prompts, bar, rail, notices) are bit-identical with the Perception Filter on or off; the only Filter-fed exception is an allow-list of mark-slot visibility properties (headless oracle: scene-state hash). | Rendering | HS-3, AC-HS-42, AC-HS-88 |
| TR-hud-005 | Exactly six reading-register node families (`suit.o2`, `suit.reserve`, `suit.integrity`, `suit.warmth`, `suit.charge`, scanner slot) are lie-capable and are read only via `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), PlayerId)` / `perceived(SCANNER, PlayerId)`; HUD modules contain zero `true_value` call sites. | Core | HS-3, HS-4, AC-PF-51 |
| TR-hud-006 | `perceived` reads fill a preallocated caller-owned `Perceived` record (`perceived(key, viewer, out)`); no record is cached across frames and steady state makes zero per-frame heap allocations. | Performance | HS-4, AC-HS-92 |
| TR-hud-007 | Non-reading suit data comes only from `Suit.view(PlayerId)` (+ `tool_in_hand`, `stowed_count`, `carried_instance`, `tool_charge`, `breath_src`); the four pre-wrap reading fields (`o2_pp_dkpa`, `reserve_pm`, `cell_pm`, `integrity_pm`) are never drawn. | Core | HS-5 |
| TR-hud-008 | The HUD's read interface is closed to the HS-6 table; it never reads Attention, Horror, Sanity state, Graph state at a distance, `peer_id`, `lit(ref)`, `loco_state`, `abort_cause`, `input_ignored_view`, or any `PERCEPTION_OUT` block. | Core | HS-6 |
| TR-hud-009 | Update model is hybrid pull: `perceived`, `focus_view`, `channel_view` and Controller reads are pulled every render frame; the discrete model rebuilds on dirty key `S/<PlayerId>` / `save_status`, and is force-rebuilt on first RUNNING frame, any restore, `ALL`-coalesced dirty (> `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256), exit from PAUSED, and any `H`/locale/glyph-device change. | Core | HS-7, ADR candidate C |
| TR-hud-010 | Animation, settle, debounce, bar fill/drain and tick phases run on `present_time` (frozen while kernel PAUSED); the mark phase, honest-numeral grid and flash-arbiter window use committed tick `T` + `tick_alpha`; layer 3 uses process time; post-pause/hitch time steps clamp at `HUD_DT_CLAMP_MS` 50 and no integrator divides by dt. | Threading/Timing | HS-8, ADR candidate B |
| TR-hud-011 | `HudLayout` outputs integer HUD-px rectangles via manual snapping (`anchor_snap`) at every `H`/display; `Control.scale` is (1,1), no node animates scale/rotation, `offset_transform_*` unused, and bars/arcs are rect/atlas fills, not `draw_line`/`draw_arc`; `gui_snap_controls_to_pixels` is never relied on. | Rendering | HS-9, D.9, AC-HS-93 |

# TRs: HUD & Suit Layer (alias: hud)

Source: design/gdd/hud-and-suit-layer.md (Presentation, MVP; systems index row 21). No ADR exists; ADR candidates A-G are listed in Overview.

| Req ID | Requirement | Domain | GDD anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| TR-hud-001 | The HUD is a `PRESENTATION`-class kernel subscriber that owns no block, hook, command, mutator, reading key, RNG stream or `INPUT_SURFACE`, and writes only CanvasItem/Material/audio-request properties. | Core | HS-1 |
| TR-hud-002 | The HUD is a `CanvasLayer` (layer 2, group `hud`) in the root viewport, never under the 640x360 world `SubViewport`; a `Control` under the world SubViewport fails the scene-tree lint (build gate). | Rendering | HS-2 |
| TR-hud-003 | HUD scale `H` is an integer in `{H_default..2*H_default}` with `H_default = max(k_auto,3)`, independent of world scale `k`; HUD code never reads `k` or assumes `H==k`; an `H` change alters no simulation value. | Rendering | HS-2, HUD_MIN_SCALE |
| TR-hud-004 | Frame-register nodes (plates, keycaps, prompts, bar, rail, notices) are bit-identical with the Perception Filter on or off; the only Filter-fed exception is an allow-list of mark-slot visibility properties (headless oracle: scene-state hash). | Rendering | HS-3, AC-HS-42, AC-HS-88 |
| TR-hud-005 | Exactly six reading-register node families (`suit.o2`, `suit.reserve`, `suit.integrity`, `suit.warmth`, `suit.charge`, scanner slot) are lie-capable and are read only via `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), PlayerId)` / `perceived(SCANNER, PlayerId)`; HUD modules contain zero `true_value` call sites. | Core | HS-3, HS-4, AC-PF-51 |
| TR-hud-006 | `perceived` reads fill a preallocated caller-owned `Perceived` record (`perceived(key, viewer, out)`); no record is cached across frames and steady state makes zero per-frame heap allocations. | Performance | HS-4, AC-HS-92 |
| TR-hud-007 | Non-reading suit data comes only from `Suit.view(PlayerId)` (+ `tool_in_hand`, `stowed_count`, `carried_instance`, `tool_charge`, `breath_src`); the four pre-wrap reading fields (`o2_pp_dkpa`, `reserve_pm`, `cell_pm`, `integrity_pm`) are never drawn. | Core | HS-5 |
| TR-hud-008 | The HUD's read interface is closed to the HS-6 table; it never reads Attention, Horror, Sanity state, Graph state at a distance, `peer_id`, `lit(ref)`, `loco_state`, `abort_cause`, `input_ignored_view`, or any `PERCEPTION_OUT` block. | Core | HS-6 |
| TR-hud-009 | Update model is hybrid pull: `perceived`, `focus_view`, `channel_view` and Controller reads are pulled every render frame; the discrete model rebuilds on dirty key `S/<PlayerId>` / `save_status`, and is force-rebuilt on first RUNNING frame, any restore, `ALL`-coalesced dirty (> `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256), exit from PAUSED, and any `H`/locale/glyph-device change. | Core | HS-7, ADR candidate C |
| TR-hud-010 | Animation, settle, debounce, bar fill/drain and tick phases run on `present_time` (frozen while kernel PAUSED); the mark phase, honest-numeral grid and flash-arbiter window use committed tick `T` + `tick_alpha`; layer 3 uses process time; post-pause/hitch time steps clamp at `HUD_DT_CLAMP_MS` 50 and no integrator divides by dt. | Threading/Timing | HS-8, ADR candidate B |
| TR-hud-011 | `HudLayout` outputs integer HUD-px rectangles via manual snapping (`anchor_snap`) at every `H`/display; `Control.scale` is (1,1), no node animates scale/rotation, `offset_transform_*` unused, and bars/arcs are rect/atlas fills, not `draw_line`/`draw_arc`; `gui_snap_controls_to_pixels` is never relied on. | Rendering | HS-9, D.9, AC-HS-93 |
| TR-hud-012 | Needle tips quantise to whole HUD px and the Filter never-rest rule (`NEVER_REST_MAX_S` 1.0 s) still holds (tip pixel changes at least once per 1.0 s at H 3 and 6; `L` 11 ineligible). | Rendering | HS-9, D.15, AC-HS-93 |
| TR-hud-013 | The surface inventory is closed (`hud_strip`, `hud_suit_panel`, `hud_rail`, `hud_prompt`+`hud_bar`, `hud_give_up_plate`, `hud_notice`, conditional `hud_aim_indicator`, inspect-card frame, reserved anchors); forbidden surfaces (minimap, health bar, Attention/sanity/horror indicators, toast, death screen, etc.) are lint-banned under any setting. | UI | HS-10 |
| TR-hud-014 | The strip's breath dial shows `suit.o2` while `breath_src` is ROOM/GASP/NONE and `suit.reserve` (whole seconds) while RESERVE; `breath_src` also selects hue and mark eligibility and is never derived from displayed values. | UI | HS-5, HS-12, AC-HS-94 |
| TR-hud-015 | Warning-mark phase is `((T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS)+tick_alpha)/BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` (`BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` 128, duty `MARK_DUTY_PM` 500), leading edge at `T mod 128 == 0` within one render frame of the audio edge, one shared phase for all six mark slots. | Threading/Timing | HS-23, D.4, AC-HS-124 |
| TR-hud-016 | While PAUSED an active mark is held ON solid, and on resume stays ON until the next leading edge (resume bridge); reduce-flashing/reduced-motion hold marks solid (reduce_flashing default ON). | Threading/Timing | HS-23, States and Transitions |
| TR-hud-017 | A single flash arbiter keyed to `T` window `(T-TICK_RATE, T]` enforces `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` over all HUD luminance events: clock-locked events never delayed, hides never deferred, deferrable events wait at most `MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 60, grid boundaries are skip-only (`GRID_MAX_CONSEC_SKIPS` 1), overruns are recorded as `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN`, never dropped, never altering the Filter's schedule. | Threading/Timing | HS-47, D.2, AC-HS-140/141 |
| TR-hud-018 | The HUD creates no simulation state and persists nothing: no HUD state is saved, replicated or hashed; on restore all presentation-local counters (debounce, grid, bar fill/drain, tick phases, flash history, device latch) are cleared and readings draw directly at restored values with no settle. | Save/Load | States and Transitions, HS-53, EC-HS-42 |
| TR-hud-019 | Save feedback is read-only: failed-write notice shows when Save/Load's `fail_escalated` (threshold `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_ESCALATE_COUNT` 3) is true and clears on `WRITTEN`; the HUD counts nothing; first-frame line shows for `UI7_DWELL_S` 8 after a fallback load or a `DEATH_STUB` restore (`restore_reason` read as request only). | Save/Load | HS-46, EC-HS-44..46 |
| TR-hud-020 | Interaction display is driven by `focus_view(seat)`, `channel_view(seat)` (local seat only), the result-event record, and Controller `confirm_view`/`glyph_view`; the bar fill is `fill_px = (hold_pm*L) div 1000` with the HUD doing no hold drain, and prompt show follows Interaction D.UI-2. | UI | HS-6, HS-37..45, D.18, D.19 |
| TR-hud-021 | The HUD issues no commands and plays no sound (zero HUD-originated audio requests at MVP); sound-request ids exist only for dormant lie slots, and the mark clock is the shared AAV-9 grid, cited not reimplemented. | Audio | HS-1, AC-HS-124 |
| TR-hud-022 | Per-frame presenter order is fixed (camera solver, Avatar Presenter, Filter, HUD, Lighting) so `world_to_hud` and `perceived` are read after their producers. | Threading/Timing | AC-HS-89, ADR candidate F |
| TR-hud-023 | HUD performance budget on RM-DESKTOP (1920x1080) and RM-DECK (1280x800, `H` 3 over `k` 2) release export: <= 60 draw calls, <= `HUD_PRIMITIVE_MAX` 90 primitives, <= `HUD_FRAME_BUDGET_US` 400 us p95 over 600 frames, atlas+needle footprint <= `HUD_MEM_CEILING_MB` 8; provisional until spike S2. | Performance | AC-HS-92, D_hud |
| TR-hud-024 | HUD maths (`strip_budget`, `hud_flash_budget`, `reserve_seconds`, `mark_phase`, `o2_dial_angle`, `bottom_row_fit`, `anchor_snap`, `cap_px`, `needle_frame_index`, etc.) are pure static functions assertable headlessly (e.g. `cap_px` H3..6 = 21,28,35,42; `side_avail` 149,102,73,53 at 1280). | Core | AC-HS-115, ADR candidate G |
| TR-hud-025 | Dial faces are baked once per layout (not per frame) and instrument faces use bitmap/atlas assets with tabular numerals; the widget approach (Control tree vs custom draw) and Theme structure are an ADR decision. | Rendering | AC-HS-92, ADR candidates A, D |
| TR-hud-026 | Tuning data lives in external `hud_tuning` data validated at load; out-of-range knobs (e.g. `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS` < 20, `HONEST_TICK_MS` != 500, `HUD_SETTLE_MS` outside 250-400, `BAR_LEN_*` not ordered S<M<L in 12-64) fail, and no gameplay-balance key may exist in it. | Data | Tuning Knobs, AC-HS-123 |
| TR-hud-027 | Nine diagnostic counters (`HUD_READ_MISSING`, `hud_perceived_oob`, `hud_unmapped_key_glyph`, `UI_MISSING_KEY`, `hud_layout_overlap`, `UI_PLACEMENT_WITHHELD`, `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN`, `hud_plate_overflow`, `hud_unknown_override`) exist, read 0 on a clean run, and are exposed via `hud_debug_snapshot()`. | Core | AC-HS-122, Dependencies (Debug Overlay) |
| TR-hud-028 | `HudSettings` hooks (opacity, reduce_flashing/flash_mode, aim_indicator, pattern strength, etc.) are consumed by the HUD but never read or written by game state; Alpha settings screens are owned elsewhere. | Data | HudSettings hooks, HR-6 |
| TR-hud-029 | Prompt plates and glyphs follow the Controller's device latch and closed `keycap_token` enumeration; unknown tokens fall back to the `?` keycap and count `hud_unmapped_key_glyph`; gamepad-only play of the core loop is fully supported. | Input | HS-6, HS-35, AC-HS-95 |
| TR-hud-030 | Missing upstream data degrades safely: a missing `perceived` record draws a blank numeral with arc at rest and increments `HUD_READ_MISSING`; the HUD never falls back to `view()` readings or invents a rule for an unowned *when*. | Core | HS-1, HS-4 |

## Public surface
- Node surfaces: `hud_strip`, `hud_suit_panel`, `hud_rail`, `hud_prompt`, `hud_bar`, `hud_give_up_plate`, `hud_notice`, `hud_aim_indicator` (conditional), reserved anchors `crew_strip`, `chat`, `caption`, `own_identity`
- `CanvasLayer` layer 2, group `hud`; Godot `Theme` and shared component set (`design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`); inspect-card frame and gleam helper
- `HudLayout` (integer HUD-px rectangles), `anchor_snap`, `HudModel` (per-frame snapshot), `HudSettings` hooks
- `hud_debug_snapshot()` read-only channel (H, picture rect, plate rectangles, mark phase, last model, nine counters)
- Dormant lie slots: gleam, glide, tick/stale, sound-request on six reading families
- Diagnostic counters: `HUD_READ_MISSING`, `hud_perceived_oob`, `hud_unmapped_key_glyph`, `UI_MISSING_KEY`, `hud_layout_overlap`, `UI_PLACEMENT_WITHHELD`, `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN`, `hud_plate_overflow`, `hud_unknown_override`
- Formulas owned: `strip_budget`, `hud_flash_budget`, `reserve_seconds`, `mark_phase`, `o2_dial_angle`, `hud_settle_response`, `nonground_count`, `bottom_row_fit`, `anchor_snap`, `safe_margin`, `integrity_zone_ticks`, `charge_fill_and_warn`, `gleam_lit_length`, `warmth_band_index`, `needle_frame_index`, `cancel_drain_fill`
- Knobs: `HUD_MIN_SCALE`, `HUD_DT_CLAMP_MS`, `MARK_DUTY_PM`, `HONEST_TICK_MS`, `HONEST_GRID_TICKS`, `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS`, `GLYPH_STATE_LATCH_TICKS`, `MAX_DEFER_TICKS`, `FLASH_AREA_EXEMPT_PM`, `HUD_SETTLE_MS`, `BAR_LEN_*`, `BAR_STROKE_PX`, `UI7_DWELL_S`, `SCAN_READING_DWELL_S`, `HUD_PRIMITIVE_MAX`, `HUD_FRAME_BUDGET_US`, `HUD_MEM_CEILING_MB`, `HUD_NONGROUND_PX_MAX`
- No commands, signals, hooks, blocks or saved state are published.

## Consumes
- Render Pipeline & Camera: layer 2, `H`, picture rect, safe margin, `world_to_hud`, `present_time`, pause state, `cap_px`, flash invariants (PR-13)
- Suit & Equipment: `view(PlayerId)` (incl. `breath_src`), `tool_in_hand`, `stowed_count`, `carried_instance`, `tool_charge`, dirty key `S/<PlayerId>`, `suit.alarm` request, warmth band edges (SE-29)
- Perception Filter: `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), PlayerId)` x5, `perceived(SCANNER, PlayerId)`, `perceived(suit.alarm)` (provisional, OQ-HS-79), `Perceived` record
- Interaction System: `focus_view(seat)`, `channel_view(seat)`, result-event record
- Player Controller & Input: `confirm_view(seat)` (`give_up_live`, `hold_pm`, `armed`, `pressed_action`, `released`), `glyph_view(seat, action)`, `keycap_token`, device latch, aim direction (16 steps)
- Save/Load: `save_status`, `fail_escalated`, fallback-load flag, `restore_reason`
- Command & Simulation Layer: `PRESENTATION` subscription, committed `T`, `tick_alpha`, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`, notifications without state
- Life-Support Graph: `O2_BAND_ANOXIC_PP`, `HYPOXIA_PP`, `O2_BAND_THIN_PP`
- Adaptive Audio & Tells: pulse-clock contract AAV-9, `ui` bus, captions slot
- Sanity: `READING_LIE_STAGE`, `SCANNER_LIE_STAGE` (via Filter only)
- Content (Boarding, Ship Assembly, Item DB, Layout): prompt tokens, `name_key`, `subject_anchors`
- Avatar Presenter (no GDD, provisional): 16 aim-step frames
- Chart Table: shared component grammar, UI-7 handoff
- Downstream: Debug Overlay (`hud_debug_snapshot`), In-World Instruments (frame, Theme, gleam helper)

## Engine risk
- `CanvasLayer` in root viewport, Control/Theme tree (Godot UI): LOW (older)
- Separate world `SubViewport` vs root viewport and integer scaling (two integer scales in one window): MEDIUM-LOW; wiring is NOT SOURCEABLE until Pipeline spike step 11
- `Control.offset_transform_*` (4.7) deliberately NOT used: HIGH (avoid)
- 4.7 line drawing has no antialiasing feather, so `draw_line`/`draw_arc` avoided for bars and dials: HIGH
- `gui_snap_controls_to_pixels`: scope unverified (spike S1/S4), not relied on: HIGH/UNV
- Custom `_draw` / atlas regions / bitmap font import and tabular numerals (spike, ADR D): LOW-MEDIUM
- GDScript per-frame allocation behavior, `_process` ordering, signal timing, text-measurement calls: NOT SOURCEABLE in pinned reference; flagged as risk (HIGH until verified)
- Renderer `forward_plus` release export performance on Steam Deck (spike S2): MEDIUM
- Accessibility (AccessKit, 4.5) for HUD accessibility notes: HIGH (Alpha, not MVP)
